axes.model_access: Adobe's own Firefly model family (image/video/sound multimodal lines) + optional third-party models inside the platform (official narrative: Firefly apps can call third-party models; not inventoried item by item); models are listed on the Adobe side.
axes.runtime: Web (firefly.adobe.com) + generative capabilities embedded in CC apps such as Photoshop/Premiere (Generative Fill etc.) — this dossier covers the standalone Firefly product line; the CC-embedded line is not listed separately per the boundary ruling (see inventory notes).
axes.local_files: Works are stored in Adobe's cloud (the Creative Cloud storage surface); no models run on your machine.
axes.background: Generation is instant/queued (the web queue varies by account tier, not verified item by item); no "keep-running-after-shutdown" task surface (no claim verified); the CC-app-embedded line runs in the app's foreground, not as a background agent.
axes.tools: The product includes text-to-image, Generative Fill/Expand, style reference, structure reference, vector recoloring (design-oriented), video generation (the Firefly video line), etc.; integration with the Adobe Stock/Express ecosystem is part of the official narrative.
axes.context: Organized by projects/libraries (CC ecosystem: integration surfaces between Firefly works and CC asset libraries exist; details not verified item by item); cross-session memory — no official statement verified.
axes.permissions: Adobe account + CC subscription system; commercial indemnification is the enterprise-facing selling point (long-standing official position); training-data stance = licensed content library (long-standing official position) — these two points are its biggest compliance differentiator from most peers.
axes.fit: Fits: enterprise compliance procurement (indemnification + licensed-training narrative), users already in the Adobe ecosystem, design-to-delivery pipelines. Does not fit: leaving the Adobe account system; wanting open weights to run locally (Firefly is not open source).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **The actual applicable tiers and scope of the indemnification clause** (check against Adobe's terms, not the marketing framing)
- **How the free allowance and the CC subscription credit pool interoperate**
- **The current list of third-party models inside Firefly** (the official narrative has not been inventoried item by item)
unknowns:
- Third-party model list (not inventoried item by item)
- Details of indemnification applicability conditions (not verified line by line)
- Cross-session memory mechanism (no official statement verified)
- The concrete composition of the "licensed content library" training data (long-standing official position; the composition has not been publicly verified item by item)
related: Both design-oriented: Recraft is a vector-native standalone bench; Firefly is embedded in the Adobe ecosystem.
Both big-vendor free design entry points: Designer is tied to the Microsoft ecosystem, Firefly to the Adobe ecosystem.
Design-workflow handoff: Firefly produces the images, Figma MCP plugs the design files into agent toolchains (cross-linked after filing).
